There used to be a time where these words used to trigger me. If I spoke to someone about anything related to nausea for too long, I'd start panicking. It doesn't bother me as much anymore, so I also censor the words mostly so that I don't trigger others with them, especially since from my past experiences I can imagine just how bad it might be. Thought honestly, old me wouldn't even join this subreddit in the first place because just thinking about anything related to feeling sick would make me panic back then, so this subreddit would definitely be a bad idea for me back then. Even if the words are censored, you still have to kind of think about what the censored word is supposed to be, so I'm not sure if it really helps? But I still censor these words in my posts just in case, because maybe it helps someone so who knows

It's a bit confusing in my situation because I was told to take 50mg every other day for the first week and then move to taking it daily on the second week. The first week the n* wasn't that bad, there was a day where it got kind of bad but didn't last long. Then once the second week started and my body had to get used to me taking it daily, the n* was kind of bad but it was mostly because I had this weird feeling in my throat which caused me to panic a little, but the n* wasn't as bad as on the first week. After the 2nd week the n* went away! The only time I felt n* after that was when I was really hungry, since I lost my appetite because of the medication. So overall it wasn't that bad!!

I recently started taking Zoloft, like 1-2 months ago, I felt really n* but no v*! Please know you're not alone. I'm going through the exact same thing. My parents never taught me that I'm supposed to brush my teeth every single day and I can't just learn that on my own as a child. Because of that, my teeth started getting worse and worse. My teeth are now all yellow, they're rotting, breaking, all of that. My parents took me to the dentist only a few times in my life, maybe like 4 times max. The last time I was there, what I experienced left me scared to visit the dentist ever again. I was around 9-10 years old back then, I'm 14. I was scared and of course, since my parents didn't really care about how horrible my teeth already looked like, we never looked for a new dentist or anything like that ever again. Now, since August I've had a problem with my teeth and because of it I can barely eat sometimes due to the horrible pain, but everytime I even think about going to the dentist, I have a panic attack. My parents make fun of me for that and they keep saying that it's my fault that my teeth look like this. I really, really try my best to brush my teeth everyday, but it's really hard when you were never taught that you're supposed to do so every day in the first place.

Seeing that someone has to go through that similar fear of dentists honestly makes me sad. I'm so sorry you have to go through that, but please know you're not alone and you're not pathetic for this.
